scope: Independent review of actual trihedral residual conormals, signed spherical cone fiber coefficient, sharp second-radius ridge fibers, and localized arbitrary-base tube moments.
findings: TrihedralResidualConormal constructs the genuine normalized double residual of the omitted basis ray after the actual bisector/difference of the other two. It proves residual nonzero, orthogonality, normalization and positive own pairing, then uses genuine Riesz-conormal uniqueness to obtain the inward orientation. No conormal identity is assumed.

TrihedralFiberBound combines the actual angle-weighted residual normals by the proved spherical balance before taking absolute values. It applies the true conical Gaussian fourth-radius fiber inequality with constant 6144*exp(3/2); no edge-count or minimum-angle factor is introduced.

SecondTubes transports the archived actual Gaussian rectangle lower bound with endpoint radius weight squared. The 1/(4R) radius and endpoint lower bound cancel the R^-2 area loss, giving the actual chord/1024 lower bound and angle coefficient constant 512*pi*exp(3/2). The separate norm-square fourth-weight bound has constant 2048*pi*exp(3/2), preserving the sharp unweighted second-moment mass.

LocalizedMoments proves the actual variable-width Gaussian tube bound by integrating first over the arbitrary probability base at fixed Gaussian residual. The true concentration hypothesis bounds the translated face layer of width sigma/R; multiplying by R^(k+1) yields sigma*R^k+delta*R^(k+1). Product integrability is proved before Fubini and integral comparison.

The outward event is a measurable subset of the actual variable tube and retains the nonnegative weight. The true three-face radius first and second moments give exp(128)*K*(sigma*sqrt(dimensionLog p)+delta*dimensionLog p), with hK,hdelta and sigma positivity used exactly when replacing moments by their bounds. No density or nonsingularity of the base is assumed.
qualifications: The reviewer did not author these four sources. Imported PositiveWedge, TrihedralBalance and earlier spherical proofs were authored by the reviewer and are disclosed dependencies, not independently re-reviewed by this record.
The polar sphere measure is the measure normalized by Euclidean volume. This record does not identify it with raw unnormalized Hausdorff measure.
The packet proves actual local coefficient/fiber and tube-moment suppliers. It does not alone supply global incidence transport or the final all-threshold Supplemental H.1 matrix theorem.
